chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Miskan, from Gassan Al-Basri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever visits the grave of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), recognizing his right, Allah will forgive him for what preceded of his sins and what followed.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn with proper recognition?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (as) to emphasize that ziyarah is not merely a physical visit but an act of spiritual recognition (ma'rifah) of the Imam's divine station. The promise of comprehensive forgiveness for both past and future sins underscores the transformative power of connecting with the Ahl al-Bayt, a concept central to Shia soteriology. This narrative reinforces the theological view that the graves of the Imams serve as intercessory sites where divine mercy is accessed through sincere devotion.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Gassan Al Basry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who comes to the grave of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> recognising his<sup>asws</sup> right, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive his sins, from the committed ones and those he will commit (in the future)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ibn Muskan from Ghassan al- Basriy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, has said that if one visits the grave of abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al- Salam, with proper understanding of his rights, Allah forgives his past sins and whatever sins come later on.”
